invariants.label: Argument Integrity
invariants.statement: Every argument node must be reachable from the argument's root claim via at least one sequence of declared structural relations. Isolated nodes — those with no relation path connecting them to the root claim — are not part of the argument structure; they are structural debris.
invariants.formal: ∀n ∈ nodes(A): ∃path p = ⟨root(A), r_1, n_1, ..., r_k, n⟩ such that ∀r_i ∈ declared_relations(A)
invariants.corollary: An argument with unreachable nodes is not a malformed argument — it is two or more disjoint structures, none of which constitutes the intended argument alone. SARG-Ν must partition nodes(A) into reachable and orphan sets before any evaluation proceeds.
invariants.violation: Counting an unreachable node as part of the argument structure; treating an orphan node's content as contributing evidence or warrant to the root claim; proceeding to evaluation when the reachability partition is incomplete.
cross_references: INV-SD-001 (Book 3 Signature Uniqueness — argument signatures require reachable nodes)

invariants.label: Warrant Necessity
invariants.statement: Every claim-evidence pair within an argument requires at least one explicit warrant relation bridging the claim node to the evidence node. An evidence node connected to a claim node without a declared warrant is a structural floating attachment — it does not structurally support the claim.
invariants.formal: ∀(c, e) ∈ claim_evidence_pairs(A): ∃w ∈ warrants(A): w.source = e ∧ w.target = c
invariants.corollary: Implicit warrants — connections assumed from context, prior discourse, or semantic proximity — are not valid under SARG. Every warrant must be explicitly declared as a structural relation before it can bear logical weight. The burden of explicitness falls on the argument constructor, not the evaluator.
invariants.violation: Accepting an evidence node as supporting a claim without a declared warrant relation; inferring warrant from semantic content of claim or evidence nodes; treating positional adjacency as a warrant substitute.
cross_references: INV-TEL-001 (Book 5 Expression Completeness — all warrants must be TEL-expressible)
INV-GRL-001 (Book 6 Regime Validity — warrant necessity parallels enforcement necessity)
invariants.tel_expression: INV[SARG-002]: assert (∀(c,e) ∈ CE_pairs(A): ∃w ∈ W(A): (e ⊢ c) ∈ declared_relations(w))

invariants.label: Defeat Completeness
invariants.statement: A defeat of an argument must target at least one structural component of that argument — a node, a declared relation, or a constraint binding — rather than merely contesting a surface-level assertion or rhetorical framing. A defeat that targets nothing structural is not a defeat; it is a parallel assertion.
invariants.corollary: Surface objections — denials of phrasing, tone, or rhetorical packaging — do not constitute structural defeats under SARG. A defeat must identify the specific structural target and demonstrate how that target's removal or revision disrupts the argument's constraint satisfaction. Uncompleted defeats are logged as parallel assertions, not as defeats.
invariants.violation: Classifying a surface objection as a structural defeat; recording a defeat without identifying a specific structural target; allowing a defeat record to modify an argument's validity status without a completed target specification.
cross_references: INV-SD-002 (Book 3 Detection Completeness — defeat requires the same null-return capacity as detection)
INV-GRL-004 (Book 6 Constraint Legitimacy — defeat channels must be declared, paralleling challenge channels)

invariants.label: Reflexive Prohibition
invariants.statement: An argument cannot provide structural support for its own root claim without passing through at least one independent evidentiary node — a node whose content and provenance are not derived from the root claim itself. Circular argument paths that return to the root claim without traversing an independent node constitute a structural self-reference violation.
invariants.formal: ¬∃path p = ⟨root(A), r_1, n_1, ..., r_k, root(A)⟩ unless ∃n_i ∈ p: independent_evidence(n_i, root(A))
invariants.corollary: A path that returns to the root claim via an independent evidentiary node is not reflexively prohibited. The prohibition targets closed loops — paths that return to root(A) having traversed only nodes derived from or equivalent to root(A). Independence of evidence is a structural property: n_i is independent of root(A) if provenance(n_i) ∩ derivation_closure(root(A)) = ∅.
invariants.violation: Allowing a circular support path without an independent evidentiary node; treating a restatement or elaboration of the root claim as an independent evidentiary node; accepting circular chains as valid structural support.
cross_references: INV-GRL-003 (Book 6 Regime Closure — self-governance parallels self-support prohibition)
INV-NOS-002 (Book 8 Relational Primacy — relations cannot derive both endpoints from one endpoint)
invariants.tel_expression: INV[SARG-004]: assert (¬∃path(root(A) → root(A)) unless (∃n_i ∈ path: independent_evidence(n_i, root(A))))
